title: LLM Voting: Human Choices and AI Collective Decision-Making

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating changes in aggregated LLM voting outcomes (measured via Kendall's tau) when the presentation order of candidate projects or their numerical IDs are reversed.

Comparing the distribution of unprompted LLM votes across different urban project categories (e.g., transportation, culture, nature) against a baseline of human votes to identify default domain preferences.
Analyzing the proportion of votes LLMs allocate to low-budget (5,000 CHF) versus high-budget (10,000 CHF) projects compared to the cost-consciousness of human voters.

Measuring the percentage of votes allocated to a persona's assigned district and category to evaluate if LLMs over-align with self-interest compared to humans' balance of self-interest and community-oriented preferences.
